title: Priv EKS Terraform bootstrap operator and health playbook
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Create a Terraform module + companion bootstrap operator that provisions and hardens the Redwood Private EKS control plane inside customer VPCs. Focus areas: idempotent bootstrap for air-gapped & cross-account VPCs, preflight/dry-run validations, CRD-based upgrade fencing, automated health probes and remediation hooks, and minimal IAM generation. The module must integrate with our existing Terraform registries and provide clear observability artifacts (metrics/logs) for Console ingestion.
acceptance_criteria: Module supports idempotent create/update/destroy across repeated runs and returns deterministic plan diffs
Preflight validation command (local) fails fast with clear remediation steps for common misconfigurations (subnet tagging, route tables, KMS permissions)
Bootstrap operator deploys in a customer-managed management namespace and exposes a CRD (PrivControlPlane) used to coordinate upgrades and health checks
Upgrade fencing: only one cluster upgrade (control-plane version change or cert rotation) can be active per control-plane CR; other requests are queued with audit annotations
Health probes emit Prometheus metrics (priv_eks_controlplane_healthy{cluster,region}) and Console dashboards show nodegroup/etcd/endpoint latencies
Module produces least-privilege IAM policies and a sealedsecret-compatible output for on-prem key-wrapping
Automated rollback: if 2 consecutive failed post-upgrade health checks occur, a documented rollback path and a postmortem checklist are created and persisted to S3-compatible customer bucket
Terraform workspace integration (optional) supports dry-run plan snapshots stored in our artifacts bucket and references in the ticket/PR
tasks: Design: define CRD schema for PrivControlPlane (operator) and alignment with Console expectations — 80%
Terraform: author module with submodules for VPC preflight, IAM, EKS cluster, nodegroups, and kms-wrapper — 40%
Operator: implement bootstrap controller (Go) for post-provisioning invariants and upgrade fencing — 25%
Observability: add metrics + logs, sample Grafana panels and Console ingestion mapping — 20%
Security review: schedule SRE/security design review for cross-account KMS usage and iam policies — TODO
E2E tests: integration harness using localstack (for S3/KMS) and kind for control-plane sanity checks — TODO
Docs: write runbook and troubleshooting playbook for SEs and SREs — TODO

risks: Air-gapped customers: operator image distribution strategy needs an offline bundle and documented install steps
Cross-account IAM: overly-broad policies could create security exposure if not audited; require automated policy linting
Upgrade failure modes: partial control-plane upgrades may leave nodegroups incompatible; need sequencer and graceful drain policy
Terraform state drift when operator reconciles resources not managed by TF: define clear ownership boundary and use annotations/tags
telemetry: Expose traces for upgrade flows (OpenTelemetry spans) to Console tracing endpoint
Archive upgrade plans and health-check snapshots to artifacts S3 for postmortem analysis
notes: Implementation plan: land minimal module that can create a hardened EKS cluster (no operator), then iterate by adding the operator in a follow-up change that takes ownership of upgrade sequencing. This reduces blast radius and allows immediate testing of Terraform idempotency. Coordinate with Console team for metric names and dashboard IDs before GA.
